newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: CRICKET-Malaysia opposition protests visiting Israeli team.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Malaysia opposition protests visiting Israeli team.

text.p: Some 300 Malaysians from an opposition Islamic party protested on Tuesday against the presence of an Israeli cricket team in Kuala Lumpur, witnesses said.
The protesters, shouting slogans against Israel and carrying placards, marched by the prime minister's office after earlier gathering at a square in central Kuala Lumpur.

The demonstrators, from the fundamentalist Malaysian Islamic Party or PAS, caused a traffic snarl in the area as police closed roads leading to the Merdeka Square, Reuters correspondents at the scene said.
Israel is making a rare sporting appearance in Asia at the International Cricket Council (ICC) Trophy being held in the Malaysian capital.
A number of protesters were allowed into the office of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad to hand over a memorandum, while the rest remained outside locked gates, witnesses said.
About half the protesters were women dressed in long-flowing Islamic gowns.
Some protesters carried placards in Malay and English that read: "We do not accept Jews in this country", "Israel get lost from Malaysia", and "Which is important: cricket or Islam".
The cricket team's visit was the first to Malaysia by an Israeli sporting team, or any other official delegation. Mainly Moslem Malaysia has no diplomatic ties with Israel.

The Malaysian Cricket Association (MCA) said it was the first visit of an Israeli sporting team to Asia since the Asia Games in Tehran in 1974, when Israel and other Middle East countries were considered part of the Asian sporting scene.
The MCA said Israel's inclusion was a condition for hosting the ICC Trophy tournament.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad had said the government wanted Israelis to see how multiracial Malaysia lived in harmony.

"We actually intend to show Israel and the Israelis that the different religious communities (in Malaysia) can live together without friction," Bernama quoted him as saying on Sunday after returning from Saudi Arabia.
